not_repaired.reason: Non-blocking. The suggested fix (record session ids in state and kill processes in those sessions at run start) carries a pid/sid-reuse risk of killing unrelated processes, so it needs a design decision rather than a minimal repair. Its main trigger (R10-01 forcing the driver to be killed) is fixed, and the remaining limit is now stated in docs/dev_workflow/URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md section 6.

report.notes: New helper lifecycle_providers.drain_after_timeout is used by run_cmd and _run: kill the group, reap the child with a time limit, sweep_orphans, then communicate with a 5 s limit, closing the pipes if a holder outside the tree remains. Tests: test_r10_01_timed_out_command_with_setsid_child_holding_stdout_returns_and_is_swept, test_r10_01_timed_out_worker_with_setsid_child_holding_stdout_returns_and_is_swept, test_r10_01_pipe_holder_outside_the_swept_tree_cannot_block_the_driver. All 3 fail on 2d419f6 (thread time limit exceeded) and pass after the change; full tests/dev_workflow: 192 passed.
